section_summary: This section details the importation, inspection, pricing, and allocation of Japanese tin stocks brought to the United States following World War II by the U.S. Commercial Company and the Reconstruction Finance Corporation under the Combined Tin Committee. Extensive diplomatic and inter-agency correspondence between the Department of State, the British and Netherlands Embassies, the RFC, and SCAP focuses on identifying looted tin of Malayan and Banka (Dutch East Indies) origin and calculating restitution and financial compensation. Later documents address SCAP's procurement of tin concentrates from Southeast Asia, Siamese tin exports, and final financial adjustments regarding sales proceeds and operational expenses.

subfiles.about: The Department of State responds to Dutch objections regarding USCC commissions, expense prorations, and the distribution of proceeds from liquidated Japanese tin.
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.summary: This memorandum replies to the Netherlands Embassy regarding expenses and proceeds from Japanese tin liquidated by the U.S. Commercial Company for SCAP. It justifies USCC's commercial commission and explains that non-Banka inspection costs are deducted before prorating remaining expenses at 51 percent for the Dutch, 42 percent for the British, and 7 percent for SCAP. State rejects the Dutch argument that former owners are entitled to US resale profits, maintaining that international allocation placed the tin into the US domestic economy and that compensation is strictly governed by the Malayan price agreements. Detailed accounting schedules show total receipts of over $16.1 million and net proceeds of $15.2 million remitted to SCAP for final restitution settlement in Tokyo.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum on Japanese Tin Accounting and Restitution
subfiles.to: Embassy of the Netherlands

subfiles.title: Netherlands Objections to USCC Deductions and Tin Expense Allocations
subfiles.to: Department of State
